forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+---
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: Rename the execute result field `lines` (a count) to `lineCount`
+---
+In the result of `tools.shell.execute`, the field `lines` is a number: how many lines the store holds for the command (Execute.swift:585, `"lines": .number(Double(stored.count))`). The text of the output is in `output` (the last lines, each "N: text").
+
+In all the sibling verbs, `lines` is an ARRAY of line texts: `tools.shell.getLines` (GetLines.swift:79), `tools.files.read` (Read.swift:99) and `tools.git.blame`. So the model reads `r.lines` of an execute result as an array, and gets a number.
+
+Evidence: SWE-bench run code-context of 2026-10-18, instance django__django-13925, transcript seq 1474-1478. The model used the `lines` of an execute result as an array of output lines, and the snippet failed.
+
+Change:
+- Rename the field to `lineCount` in `Execute.reportFields`. This name agrees with `exitCode` and `durationMs`, and a number with the name `lineCount` cannot look like an array.
+- Do not keep `lines` as an alias. A count with the name `lines` is the fault.
+- Update the doc comments, the verb description, the README and each test that reads the field. `outputNote` ("Showing the last N of M lines") stays.
+- Look at all other result shapes of the shell verbs (the pending notice, the final result of a pending snippet, the `did not finish` text) for the same field, and rename it there too.
+
+TDD: first a failing test that an execute result has `lineCount` equal to the count of stored lines and has no `lines` key. Then the change. One full `swift test` run.
+
+After the push, the FoundationModelsACPAgent repo must update the fixture in .claude/skills/swebench/scripts/test_scan.py:217 (it writes `"lines": len(lines)` for an execute result). The scan reads `output`, so it does not break. #tools
\ No newline at end of file
